examples: What's your cell number?
My number ends in zero.
I only want one.
note: Before a noun: un (un taco), una (una cerveza).

examples: Two coffees, please.
I have three siblings.
There are four of us in my family.
I'll be there in five minutes.
The class starts at six.
A week has seven days.
I work eight hours a day.
The bank opens at nine.
It's ten pesos.
My son is eleven years old.
See you at twelve.
I live at number thirteen.
February 14 is the Day of Love and Friendship.
The fifteenth-birthday party is very important in Mexico.
note: Quinceañera = a girl celebrating her 15th birthday, and also the big party itself.

examples: My daughter is sixteen years old.
note: 16–19 are written as one word: dieciséis, diecisiete, dieciocho, diecinueve.

examples: Wait for me twenty minutes.
note: 21–29 are written as one word: veintiuno, veintidós, veintitrés…

examples: I'm thirty years old.
note: From 31 on they're written with “y”: treinta y uno, cuarenta y dos.

examples: The house is forty minutes from downtown.
It cost me fifty pesos.
An hour has sixty minutes.
My grandpa is seventy years old.
My grandma is eighty years old and still cooks.
I only have ninety pesos.
There are a hundred people at the party.
The ticket costs a thousand pesos.
note: It doesn't change: dos mil = two thousand.

examples: More than nine million people live in Mexico City.
note: It's followed by “de”: un millón de pesos.

examples: It's the first time I've come to Mexico.
note: Before a masculine noun: primer (el primer día).

examples: I live on the second floor.
note: As a noun: un segundo = a second. “Un segundo, por favor” = One moment, please.

examples: It's the third time I've called you.
note: Before a masculine noun: tercer (el tercer piso).

examples: It's the last bus of the night.
Wait for me half an hour.
note: y media = half past: a las dos y media = at half past two.

examples: I want half.
I bought a dozen eggs.
What percentage do you leave as a tip in Mexico?
The unemployment figures improved.
My son is seventeen.
That's eighteen pesos.
We live at number nineteen.
The book has two hundred pages.
note: Hundreds agree in gender: doscientos pesos, doscientas personas.

examples: Admission costs five hundred pesos.
The flight costs seven hundred dollars.
We paid nine hundred pesos for electricity.
It's a quarter past three.
I live on the fourth floor.
He came in fifth place.
My daughter is in sixth grade.
I bought a pair of shoes.
Now it costs twice as much.
There was a huge number of people.
It's about a two-hour trip.
There's a ten percent discount.
This is the tenth time I've told you.
Most of my friends live nearby.
Only a minority voted against it.
Seven is an odd number.
According to statistics, people read less.

note: Careful: un billón = a trillion. A billion = mil millones.

examples: I did a quick calculation.
Hundreds of people came.
